## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sumaṅgalattheraapadāna* is a verse text situated within the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the biographical narrative and past meritorious deeds of the elder Sumaṅgala. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the poem across five languages [SuttaCentral].
Although SuttaCentral records no curated external parallels [SuttaCentral], DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse involving 100 matching passages across 12 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse correspondences are found with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, both parts 1 and 2), which quotes or shares numerous verses with this text (such as §10.4–11.3) [DharmaNexus]. A shared verse sequence (§5.4–6.2) also appears in the *Āṭānāṭiya Sutta* (DN 32) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, formulaic stanzas in segments §17–19 recur widely throughout other poems in the *Therāpadāna*, including the *Raṭṭhapālattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 20), *Mahāmoggallānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 4), *Khomadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 32), and *Subhūtittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 23) [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* (scoring up to 75) and portions of the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
